name: PSFplayers photo set + measured.csv face measurements
stated_by: unknown - the set was assembled before this project and carries no manifest
note: 26,138 jpgs named Firstname_Lastname.jpg, plus measured.csv with per-face colour. An all-time set, not modern-only: verified 2026-09-04 by finding Chick Maggioli (an obscure 1950 back) present.

THE_ONLY_KEY_IS_A_NAME.problem: this source carries NO birth date, NO club, NO season and NO id. A name is the entire identity claim it can make, and design 2.4 forbids a name as identity evidence.
THE_ONLY_KEY_IS_A_NAME.what_makes_it_usable_at_all: a name that denotes EXACTLY ONE person in the whole 40,745-person universe is not a name match; it is a name plus the verified absence of an alternative. That verification is the discriminator, and it is recorded as such.
THE_ONLY_KEY_IS_A_NAME.tier: 3 - weaker than a source-native id and weaker than name+birth_date. It rests on the corpus being complete enough for uniqueness to mean something, which it is not for men who never appear in it.
THE_ONLY_KEY_IS_A_NAME.THE_LIMIT_TO_CARRY_EVERYWHERE_COVERAGE_I: Uniqueness is verified against OUR universe, not the world. If a photo is of a man we do not hold, and a same-named man we DO hold is unique here, the photo attaches to the wrong person and NOTHING FIRES. The 20,779 figure carries this assumption and must never be quoted without it.

hard_rules: A photo whose name denotes MORE THAN ONE person is REFUSED. It is not attached to the likeliest man.
A photo whose name denotes NOBODY is REFUSED. It is not normalised until it matches.
No normalisation. Stripping middle initials, punctuation or generational suffixes converts a non-match into a match by discarding the only distinguishing information the filename carries.

normalisation_DECLINED._the_reason_is_stronger_than_information: A middle initial is not merely detail being discarded. It is EVIDENCE THAT AMBIGUITY EXISTS IN THE PHOTO SET'S OWN UNIVERSE. Somebody filed 'michael m_lewis' rather than 'michael_lewis' because there was another Michael Lewis to distinguish him from. Stripping it discards the WARNING, not just the detail.

MEASURED_2026_09_04._what_that_proves: the set distinguishes these men ITSELF. 'reggie e white' and 'reggie white' are both present, as are 'jim w kelly' and 'jim kelly'. The initial is a disambiguator, demonstrated rather than assumed.

THE_18.what_happens: both photos attach to the SAME person, so one of them is another man's face, rendered with no error anywhere
examples: paul c johns vs paul johns
tim a watson vs tim watson
john r gilliam vs john gilliam
ray r hayes vs ray hayes
derek g smith vs derek smith
al a jackson vs al jackson
THE_18.note: our corpus holds ONE Paul Johns. The source holds TWO photos. The source knows something our person universe does not.

MEASURED_2026_09_04.and_613_of_657: the bare name is ambiguous - independent confirmation that initials in this set mark exactly the names that need distinguishing

normalisation_DECLINED.CORRECTION: report 28 said normalisation would gain 597 and described the misses as 'systematic: middle initials, two-part forenames, punctuation'. The 597 came from punctuation and Jr/Sr only - the normaliser never stripped a middle initial, so that group was never in the 597. Measured separately, stripping initials would gain at most 13 safe matches and 18 dangerous ones.

absence_semantics.status_no_face: measured.csv rows with status 'no face' are an ABSENCE claim: the image was processed and no face was found. 5,131 of 9,472 measured rows.
absence_semantics.photo_not_held: a person with no photo is an absence of the SOURCE, declared here, not one absence claim per man
